work.agent_query: Read README.md. You are a taxi-fleet revenue analyst as of 2025-12-31. Write strategy/policy.py: allocate(universe, asof) -> {entity_id: weight}, spreading a FINITE growth book across the 2,402 eligible Chicago licensed taxis using the boundary feature table (YoY trip_total receipt growth at several horizons, its acceleration, recent momentum, volume/size, share, volatility, trend). The judge runs your policy once and grades how much of the taxis' ACTUALLY REALIZED Mar-May 2026 YoY receipt growth your budget sat in front of (a hidden future window), on three lanes: coverage hit rate vs the universe median, top-decile tail capture, and growth captured vs the equal-weight benchmark. The book TARGETS the growth tail (higher realized growth is better; higher capture is better). The starter IS the equal-weight budget and scores exactly 0.00. Copying boundary_yoy is weak (rank persistence is only +0.25), and allocating to the largest-volume taxis realizes a WORSE capture than the benchmark -- measured, not hypothetical. Per-taxi weight is capped at 0.0066666667 (= 1/150), so a legal book holds at least 150 names. Also write strategy/book_report.json describing the book you submit: the judge recomputes every statistic from your weights and ZEROES your score if you misreport. Offline; policy.py passes a static ALLOWLIST gate -- only pure stdlib maths modules and taxi_scorer import; no filesystem, no os/json/csv/numpy/random/time, no open/eval/exec/getattr. Rehearse book shape with `python3 check.py`; it cannot preview your grade (the graded window is hidden by construction).
